name: Turks and Caicos Islands
flagName: Flag of the Turks and Caicos Islands
summary: A British blue ensign with the islands' shield: a queen conch shell, a spiny lobster and a Turk's head cactus on gold.
origin: Earlier colonial badges showed a ship and salt rakers. The current arms were granted in 1965 and added to the blue ensign in 1968; the shield was enlarged in 1999.

symbols.name: Queen conch
symbols.meaning: Marine life and fishing, a mainstay of the economy.

symbols.name: Spiny lobster
symbols.description: A lobster in the centre of the shield.

symbols.name: Turk's head cactus
symbols.description: A cactus with a red, fez-like top.
symbols.meaning: The cactus that gave the Turks Islands their name.

facts: The Turks Islands are named after the Turk's head cactus, whose top resembles a fez.
An early version of the colonial badge famously showed salt piles drawn as igloos, an error by a London artist.
Conch is the islands' national dish.
clues: A blue ensign with a gold shield showing a conch, a lobster and a cactus.
Its islands are named after a cactus shaped like a fez.
An old badge mistakenly drew salt piles as igloos.
